# tokens: # class — nominal type with fields, inheritance, and instantiation
# `class {field:Type …}` builds a class type — boru's
# inheritance-aware type form. Class types can be:
#   - anonymous       — `class {a:String}` produces an unnamed
#                       Type with an internal ID (Class/T_…).
#   - named           — `def Foo (class {a:String})` installs Foo
#                       on the type stack.
#   - inheriting      — `def Bar (refine Foo {b:Integer})` extends
#                       Foo with new fields. The result type ID is
#                       `Class/Foo/Bar` and the instance carries
#                       both Foo's and Bar's field constraints.
# Instantiation goes via `make NAME data`. The result is a typed
# class instance that:
#   - renders as `Class/<path>{k:v,…}`,
#   - reports `typeof` as the named type,
#   - supports dotted field access (`.field`),
#   - satisfies parent-type `is` checks.
# Field validation: `make` checks that `data` carries every required
# field with values that satisfy each declared type. Missing fields
# raise an error.
# Runs against the production lang registry (test/go/langspec).
# === Test fixtures (q-suffixed spec-runner words) ===
#   addq    — [Number Number] forward-prec — args[1] + args[0]
#   lengthq — [List] forward-prec — list length
# === end fixtures ===
# 1. Anonymous class types
# `class {fields}` produces a Type with a synthesized
# internal name (Class/T_…). The exact ID is non-deterministic, so
# this section relies on type-stable assertions (typeof, is) rather
# than literal string comparison.
# An anonymous Type reports its `typeof` as a synthesised name
# (Class/T_xxx) — the internal ID used to disambiguate anonymous
# instances. Tests can't pin the exact ID, so this section uses
# named types in subsequent rows. Bare construction succeeds:
lengthq [ class { a:Integer } ]
note: the constructor produces exactly one stack value

note: multi-field anonymous still produces one value

# 2. Named class types via `def NAME (class {…})`
# `def NAME class {…}` binds the named class type; once bound
# the bare name resolves to the Type value at that name.
def Foo (class { a:String }) typeof Foo
note: typeof is one Parent hop uniformly (§6; NUR094 retired): a root class answers Class; the self-name question is `canon Foo`

# tokens: def Foo (class { a:String b:Boolean }) typeof Foo
note: multi-field named type — same uniform hop

# tokens: # 3. Instantiation via `make`
# `make NAME data` validates each declared field against `data` and
# returns a typed class instance.
def Foo (class { a:String }) make Foo { a:'hi' } typeof
note: the made value's typeof is the type name

# tokens: def Foo (class { a:String b:Integer }) make Foo { a:'hi' b:9 } typeof
# Missing required field → error.
def Foo (class { a:String }) make Foo { }
# 4. Field access via dotted accessor
# Class instances support the same `.field` syntax that maps do.
def Foo (class { a:String }) ( make Foo { a:'hi' } ) .a
def Foo (class { a:String b:Integer }) ( make Foo { a:'x' b:7 } ) .a
def Foo (class { a:String b:Integer }) ( make Foo { a:'x' b:7 } ) .b
# Chained field access — an instance whose field is another instance.
def Inner (class { v:Integer }) def Outer (class { i:Inner }) ( make Outer { i:( make Inner { v:99 } ) } ) .i .v
# 5. Inheritance
# `def Child (refine Parent {fields})` makes Child inherit from
# Parent. The full type path is `Class/Parent/Child` and Child
# instances carry both sets of fields.
# Path / structure inspection — typeof reports the most-specific name.
def Foo (class { a:String }) def Bar (refine Foo { b:Integer }) typeof Bar
note: typeof of a subclass is its parent class (§6 uniform hop)

# tokens: # A Bar instance satisfies Foo (parent) via `is`.
def Foo (class { a:String }) def Bar (refine Foo { b:Integer }) make Bar { a:'x' b:9 } is Foo
# Multi-level inheritance.
def A (class { a:Integer }) def B (refine A { b:Integer }) def C (refine B { c:Integer }) make C { a:1 b:2 c:3 } is A
def A (class { a:Integer }) def B (refine A { b:Integer }) def C (refine B { c:Integer }) make C { a:1 b:2 c:3 } typeof
# Inherited field access — Foo's `a` is reachable on a Bar instance.
def Foo (class { a:String }) def Bar (refine Foo { b:Integer }) ( make Bar { a:'x' b:9 } ) .a
def Foo (class { a:String }) def Bar (refine Foo { b:Integer }) ( make Bar { a:'x' b:9 } ) .b
# 6. Composition with def
# A made instance can be captured by `def`. The bound name then
# substitutes the instance value at every use site.
def Foo (class { a:String }) def f ( make Foo { a:'hi' } ) f .a
note: def-captured class instance preserves type & fields

# tokens: def Foo (class { a:Integer }) def f ( make Foo { a:42 } ) f .a addq 8
# 7. Multiple instances
# Each `make` call yields a fresh class instance; they're independent.
def Foo (class { a:Integer }) def x (make Foo { a:1 }) def y (make Foo { a:2 }) ( x .a ) addq ( y .a )
